newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks finish up, boosted by CITIC talk.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks finish up, boosted by CITIC talk.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks finished strong on Tuesday, rebounding after five straight losing sessions and spurred by talk that CITIC Pacific may buy a stake in China Light and Power, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index rose 108.39 points, or 0.82 percent, to 13,403.29, after climbing to a session high of 13,450.56.

Trading in CITIC Pacific and China Light shares was suspended. "The big news event today has been the suspension of CITIC and China Light and lots of rumours about what will happen. Most of them involve CITIC taking a stake in China Light," said Archie Hart, director at BZW Asia.
He said although the market had begun on a weak note on Tuesday, expectations of a CITIC deal soon turned that around.
Analysts said a link would be positive for both companies, allowing CITIC to continue its diversification while China Light would have a partner in China.

"It is particularly good news whatever happens to China Light," said Hart. "Someone has taken an interest in it, and for the utility sector, which for 1996 was awful, it looks like we have two big deals in the first few weeks of 1997."
Hutchison raised its stake in Hongkong Electric earlier this month, triggering a general offer for the utility company.
Utilities Hongkong and China Gas and Hongkong Telecom were strong on Tuesday, gaining HK$0.15 to HK$14.65 and HK$0.45 to HK$13.15 respectively. HK Electric was unchanged at HK$26.80.
Overall turnover on Tuesday was slightly higher than Monday's at HK$8.64 billion compared with HK$8.61 billion.
OCBC Securities associate director Peter Lai said it seemed as if the market had completed its consolidation.
"All the fundamentals remain positive so I believe that the market at this time can try to test 13,800 this week," he said.
Ricky Tam, senior research analyst at Delta Asia Securities, said the Hang Seng Index may test 13,500 over the next few days.
"But I think after futures expiry (on Thursday) we could see profit-taking," he said.
January Hang Seng futures rose 160 points to 13,365.
Hart said the local market would watch Wall Street closely.
"With the long bond yield near seven percent, the market is going nowhere unless the long bond and Wall Street pick themselves up off the floor," he said.
Shares in Asia Securities rose HK$0.90 to HK$2.65. It said it was considering spinning off its China business.
Giordano rose HK$0.225 to HK$4.025 after falling nearly 25 percent on Monday. -- Jennifer Genevieve (852) 2843 6345
